text:
Priya Shah: quick question — when the gateway routes to a fallback model variant (eg. quantized v2) because of capacity, should quota/cost attribution stay with the original tenant or be attributed to the gateway/pooled capacity? console shows weird token spikes and customers get confused.
Alex Kim: current runtime sends the request as-is and we annotate spans with a routing tag, but the billing pipeline uses the executor that served the tokens -> so it attributes to the model instance. that ends up splitting cost across tenant+pool.
Mateo Rivera: +1 that splitting is what we do today. It was easier for infra to bill at execution time. downside: tenants see unpredictable unit costs.
Sophie Li: from UX perspective we want a single owner in the console for cost & quota. split attribution breaks quota alerts and makes rollouts noisy.
Priya Shah: ideally we'd preserve "logical owner" for quota enforcement/alerts and record a separate "execution account" for infra chargeback. two surfaces: tenant-facing quota and infra-facing chargeback.
Alex Kim: technically we can propagate an X-Logical-Owner header and ensure meter writes use that when emitting tenant metrics. but risk: if fallback changes semantics we might undercount or double-charge.
Mateo Rivera: also need to decide where to enforce quotas. gateway-level throttles are cheap/fast. if we enforce at execution, we can better handle tenant-specific SLOs. both have tradeoffs.
Jordan (prodeng): for incidents we need traceability — when a fallback happens we should emit: route_decision=fallback, fallback_reason=capacity, exec_account=pixel-pool-3, logical_owner=tenant-42. that lets billing/console join on trace_id.
Priya Shah: agreed. what about UX for rollouts? when we do canary -> some requests will hit new variant. customers must see a clear diff in console (tokens by variant).
Sophie Li: show a split view: primary attribution to tenant but allow an "Execution details" panel that shows which model/variant served tokens and the infra account. default view stays tenant-centric.
Alex Kim: implementation proposal:
- gateway adds headers: X-Logical-Owner, X-Route-Decision, X-Route-Reason
- runtime writes two meters: tenant_meter(<logical_owner>, tokens) and infra_meter(<exec_account>, tokens)
- tracing: add attributes route.variant, route.policy, route.exec_account

code sketch:
```
headers := map[string]string{
  "X-Logical-Owner": req.TenantID,
  "X-Route-Decision": "fallback",
  "X-Route-Reason": "capacity_surge",
}
client.Do(req.WithHeaders(headers))
```

and proto telemetry message:
```
message RouteEvent {
  string trace_id = 1;
  string tenant = 2; // logical owner
  string exec_account = 3; // infra billing
  string variant = 4;
  string policy = 5;
}
```

Mateo Rivera: sounds good. slight caution: quota enforcement must consult tenant_meter in realtime. if gateway delegates to runtime, we need a fast path to sync local counters or a token-bucket lease RPC.
Priya Shah: lease RPC idea is promising: gateway asks quota service for a tokens lease before routing heavy requests. if lease fails, we short-circuit with 429. reduces overbilling.
Jordan (prodeng): also want a console flag for "show infra chargeback" so finance can opt-in to see infra attribution. default off for tenants.
Sophie Li: UX checklist from this thread: default tenant view (single owner), an optional infra chargeback toggle, execution details panel, and clear labels for fallback vs primary.
Alex Kim: ops note — add telemetry sampling for these events initially (1%) then bump on rollout. avoid racking up metrics during canary. deploy-bot: canary started for gateway v2 -> id: canary-2026-03-21-03
Priya Shah: plan: i'll draft a short RFC capturing header contract, meter semantics, quota-lease flow, and console UX changes. can we aim for review by EOD tomorrow?
Mateo Rivera: i'm in for the infra meter and lease RPC sections.
Sophie Li: i'll sketch mockups for execution details and the toggle.
Alex Kim: i'll prototype header propagation in the shim and a debug endpoint to replay route events.
Jordan (prodeng): i'll outline the join keys for billing/trace correlation.
Priya Shah: thanks all. tagging follow-ups: @Alex Kim please include fallback_reason enums; @Jordan (prodeng) make sure billing team ok with separate exec_account. :thumbsup:
